blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule VII - Parking Requirements">


Reason for Two Versions: The 2004 Revised IRR significantly updated parking requirements from the original 1977 PD 1096 — introducing urbanization tiers, vehicle-type-specific slots, and GFA-bracket differentiation.[web:2][web:4] Many reviewers and exam question banks were written before or without reflecting the 2004 revision. The board exam draws from both pools. This module presents both versions side by side.


</LawCallout>

blocks.raw:
<Callout variant="authority" title="Reason for the Law">

The 2.50 m perpendicular width accommodates modern vehicle widths plus a minimum door-opening clearance.[web:2][web:12] The parallel slot is longer (6.00 m vs. 5.00 m) because the arc of parallel entry requires additional fore-and-aft buffer.[web:2][web:12] The accessible slot’s extra width provides a dedicated wheelchair transfer zone and an adequate adjacent walkway so a wheelchair can maneuver beside the parked vehicle without encroaching into traffic or other slots.[file:16]

</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Callout variant="authority" title="22 sq.m.) are purchased primarily by young professionals or as investment units">

Studio apartments (18–22 sq.m.) are purchased primarily by young professionals or as investment units — statistically low car-ownership cohorts. Requiring 1:1 parking for every studio would price affordable housing out of the market. The graduated sclea (8→6→4→1) reflects the empirical relationship between unit size and vehicle ownership.[web:6][web:10]

</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Callout variant="authority" title="Reason for the Law">

The 4.00 m width (with 1.20 m walkway) provides generous lateral clearance for wheelchair deployment and maneuvering without forcing users into traffic lanes.[file:16] The stepped ratio table scleas accessible provision with facility size and switches to percentage and “+1 per 100 or fraction thereof” at larger counts to maintain proportionality in very large parking facilities.[file:16]

</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Callout variant="authority" title="Reason for the Law">

"Or fraction thereof" is a deliberate legislative choice to prevent under-provision through rounding. A fraction of a slot represents a real car that has no place to park, so the law mandates that the developer absorb the cost of the additional slot rather than leaving one car without parking.[web:6][web:10]

</Callout>

blocks.raw: Reveal Answer **Correct Answer: C — 5 slots** **Analysis:** - Step 1: 45 sq.m. falls in the **">22.00 up to 50.00 sq.m."** bracket under Division A-2 (R-5 Condominium), amended by DPWH DO 059 s. 2019.[web:6][web:10] - Step 2: Ratio = 1 pooled slot per **6 units** (or fraction thereof).[web:6][web:10] - Step 3: 25 units ÷ 6 = **4.167** → round UP to **5 slots**.[web:6][web:10] - Option D (4 slots) is the classic rounding-down error — the "fraction thereof" rule requires rounding up. - Option B (6 slots) would be the result of applying the 1:4 ratio (50–100 sq.m. bracket) — wrong bracket.[web:6][web:10]

blocks.raw: Reveal Answer **Correct Answer: B — 9 car slots + 2 bus slots** **Analysis:** - The 2004 Revised IRR specifies: 1 car slot per **3 rooms** (highly urbanized city) + **2 tourist bus slots** per hotel (flat requirement).[web:2][web:12] - Car slots: 25 ÷ 3 = 8.33 → round UP to **9 car slots** ("or fraction thereof").[web:2][web:12] - Bus slots: **2 tourist bus slots** — this is a flat per-hotel requirement regardless of room count.[web:2][web:12] - Option C (3 car slots) would represent 25 ÷ 3 rounded down — wrong direction. - Option A omits the mandatory bus slots entirely.

blocks.raw: Reveal Answer **Correct Answer: D — 2.50 m x 5.00 m** **Analysis:** - Per Rule VII, Sec. 707.4 of the PRBoA-annotated 2004 Revised IRR: the minimum size for a perpendicular or diagonal automobile parking slot is **2.50 m x 5.00 m**.[web:2][web:12] - Option A (2.00 x 5.00) appears in older pre-2004 references — not the current standard.[web:4] - Option B (2.15 x 6.00) is the **parallel** parking slot dimension — a deliberate distractor.[web:2][web:12] - Option C (2.40 x 5.00) appears in some unofficial reviewers — not the IRR figure.[web:4]

blocks.raw: Reveal Answer **Correct Answer: C — 3 slots** **Analysis (using Table A.6.1, Amended BP 344 Appendix A):** - BP 344 Appendix A, Table A.6.1 specifies: - 151–200 total slots → **6 accessible slots** for that band, but note the bands are cumulative from 1 upwards.[file:16] - The exam-friendly way to see 180 slots: - 1–25 → 1 slot - 26–50 → 2 slots - 51–75 → 3 slots - 76–100 → 4 slots - 101–150 → 5 slots - 151–200 → 6 slots - For **180 total slots**, you are in the **151–200** band, so the minimum required is **6 accessible slots**.[file:16] > If you want a simplified heuristic, remember: once you cross 150 slots, you are already at **5 accessible slots**, and any total up to 200 pushes you to **6 accessible slots**, not just 2.[file:16]
